title: Transcription Post-Recording Pipeline
requirements: Add DiaryStore.setTranscript(for id: UUID, source: TranscriptSource, text: String) async throws that writes the transcript text into the entry's .md file via temp-write + osrename (same atomic pattern as append), then updates entry.source and entry.updatedAt in manifest.json in place

Construct a single shared TranscriptionService at app startup with a WhisperClient built from the current Keychain API key (nil when unset); inject it into RecordingViewModel via a constructor parameter — never default-construct a Recorder-only service inside the view-model

After AudioRecorder.stop() returns a valid non-empty URL in RecordingViewModel.stop(), call service.transcribe(at: url) and iterate the AsyncStream<TranscriptUpdate>; set isFinalizing = true while streaming and false on .partial/.final/.failed
On .final(Transcript): call store.setTranscript with the final text and source, set completedEntry, invoke onCompleted

On .failed: set a typed error state on RecordingViewModel (e.g. transcriptionError: RecorderError/TranscriptionError); persist the entry with source .none and empty transcript OR surface the error — never build a DiaryEntry from an empty URL

Guard persistence: never call FileManager.moveItem(at: URL(filePath: "")) — audioPath must be non-empty before DiaryEntry construction; Document the AudioRecorder.stop() contract as throwing RecorderError.notRecording when not active
acceptance_criteria: Stopping a 5-second recording yields a non-empty transcript within 10 seconds for a normal installation (faster on-device if Speech succeeds; longer for Whisper fallback)
After transcription, manifest.json shows the updated source and updatedAt, and the .md file contains the transcript text
Stopping without start() produces no completedEntry and no UI side-effects (typed RecorderError.notRecording)
Transcript writes are atomic (temp + rename) so a crash mid-write leaves a consistent prior state
